name.text: Find the rate at which the population is growing when 𝑡=a

questiontext.text:
A population of \({@a_1@}\) bacteria is introduced into a culture and grows according to the equation 

\( \displaystyle p(t) = {@fx@}\)

where \(t\) is measured in hours. Find the rate at which the population is growing when \(t={@dd@}\).

Give your correct answer to \(2\) decimal places.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

To find the rate at which the population is growing when \(t = {@dd@} \), we need to calculate the derivative of the population function \(p(t)\) with respect to time \(t\) and then evaluate it at \(t = {@dd@}\).

The given population growth equation is:

\[p(t) = {@fx@} \]

To find \( \displaystyle \frac{dp}{dt} \), we will differentiate this equation using the quotient rule, which states that for a function \( \displaystyle u(t) =\frac{ f(t)}{g(t)} \), the derivative \( \displaystyle \frac{du}{dt} \) is given by:

\[ \displaystyle \frac{du}{dt} = \frac{f'(t)g(t) - f(t)g'(t)}{[g(t)]^2}\]

In our case, \( \displaystyle f(t) = {@numer@} \) and \(g(t) = {@denom@} \).

Now, let's calculate the derivatives:

\(1. f'(t) = {@diff((numer),t)@} \) (the derivative of \({@numer@}\) with respect to \(t\)).

\(2. g'(t) = {@diff(denom,t)@} \) (the derivative of \({@denom@}\) with respect to \(t\)).

Now, apply the quotient rule to \(p(t)\):

\[ \displaystyle p'(t) = {@a_1@} \left( \frac{({@diff((numer),t)@})({@denom@}) - ({@numer@})({@diff(denom,t)@})}{({@denom@})^2} \right) \]

Simplify this expression:

\[ \displaystyle p'(t) = {@a_1@} \left( \frac{ {@diff((numer),t)*denom@} - {@numer*diff(denom,t)@}}{({@denom@})^2} \right) \] \[p'(t) = {@dfx@} \]

Now, we want to find \(p'({@dd@})\), which is the rate at which the population is growing when \(t = {@dd@} \):

calculating this expression:

\[ \displaystyle p'({@dd@}) \approx {@ta@}\]

So, the rate at which the population is growing when \(t = {@dd@}\) is approximately \({@decimalplaces(ta,2)@}\), rounded to two decimal places.
